hypotheses.expected_result: A substantial reduction in 8T50 frequency and fresh pairs from one or more entirely uncovered imprimitive groups, with several signatures possible inside the same construction.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Reject the hypothesis if screening across fresh seeds yields no non-8T50 verified field, or if more than 90% of verified outputs collapse to a single transitive group despite the modular and signature stratification.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Generic compositions F(x)=G(H(x)), where H=x^2+ux+v is monic quadratic and G is monic quartic, will replace the baseline's S8 concentration by groups contained in the imprimitive wreath product C2 wr S4. Varying ramification and modular cycle fingerprints should expose multiple currently absent 8T groups rather than one isolated family.
hypotheses.implementation: Derive independent deterministic streams from seed. Sample u,v and quartic coefficients from several expanding integer scales, form the composition exactly in ascending coefficient order, and reject zero constant terms and duplicates. Use lightweight finite-field factorization at several small unramified primes to retain a balanced collection of admissible factor-degree fingerprints, including irreducible reductions when available, rather than accepting only the most common pattern. Stratify candidates by exact Sturm real-root count 0,2,4,6,8 and by simple ramification features such as discriminant valuations. Increase parameter scales deterministically whenever a stratum cannot fill, guaranteeing exactly budget outputs.
hypotheses.label: Generic quadratic-composition wreath search
hypotheses.mission: Attack entirely missing imprimitive groups by forcing a four-block system while preserving enough parameter freedom to realize several transitive subgroups.
hypotheses.rationale: Every root of G has a two-element fiber under H, giving a Galois-invariant partition into four pairs. Unlike even-polynomial sampling, allowing a linear term in H and unrestricted quartic coefficients avoids unnecessary global sign symmetry and permits the independent fiber swaps characteristic of the full wreath product and its subgroups. All such groups are entirely missing from the measured catalogue.

hypotheses.expected_result: Repeated fresh-seed hits on 8T50|8, completing the signature coverage of the incumbent group; low-height center sets may also yield a competitive totally real field discriminant.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Reject the hypothesis if at least 95% of generated vectors certify as having eight real roots but no 8T50|8 hit appears in preliminary fresh-seed evaluation, indicating that the construction systematically lands in another group or is too often reducible.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Small perturbations of polynomials with eight well-separated integral roots can produce irreducible totally real octics whose generic Galois group is S8, filling 8T50|8 far more reliably than coefficient-box sampling.
hypotheses.implementation: Generate eight distinct irregular centers from seed, sort them, and expand their spacing deterministically. Form P exactly, then try small constant or affine perturbations L(x)=sx+t. Certify eight simple real roots using Sturm counts or rational sign-isolating intervals; reject failures, zero constant terms, and duplicates. Favor candidates exhibiting, at distinct good primes, factor-degree patterns corresponding to an 8-cycle, a 7-cycle with a fixed point, and a transposition-like pattern; use partial-pattern tiers if the strict tier fills too slowly. Draw centers, perturbations, primes, and scale order procedurally from seed and continue until exactly budget unique vectors are obtained.
hypotheses.label: Certified totally real S8 completion
hypotheses.mission: Attack the sole missing signature in the partially covered group 8T50, namely 8T50|8.
hypotheses.rationale: The incumbent already finds 8T50 with r=0,2,4,6, so only a root-geometry constraint is missing. For P(x)=product_i(x-c_i) with irregular, widely separated integers c_i, suitable small nonzero perturbations P(x)+L(x) retain eight real roots while destroying the reducibility of P. Modular cycle patterns can strongly favor S8 without hard-coding a target polynomial.

hypotheses.expected_result: New verified pairs in direct-product or diagonal imprimitive groups not favored by generic composition, particularly signatures r=0,4,8, with occasional low-discriminant composita when q and d are small.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Reject the hypothesis if verified fraction is below 20% or every verified output is 8T50. If one non-8T50 group dominates, retain the construction only if varying quartic modular fingerprints demonstrably produces a second group or a new signature.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Norm polynomials F(x)=q(x+sqrt(d))q(x-sqrt(d)), with q a procedural irreducible quartic and d nonsquare, will often define degree-8 composita whose Galois action is close to Gal(q) x C2. The quadratic involution acts simultaneously across four pairs, a much smaller and different action from the independent pair swaps in Candidate A, so it should reach different entirely missing 8T groups.
hypotheses.implementation: Procedurally generate primitive monic quartics q with nonzero discriminant and varied small coefficients. Use modular factor patterns to favor quartic S4, A4, D4, or cyclic-like behavior without naming catalogue octics. Generate signed squarefree d from an expanding deterministic sequence and symbolically multiply the two conjugate translates so all irrational terms cancel. Reject square d, zero octic constant term, duplicate vectors, and obvious degree drops; optionally test degree eight by exact rational factorization when available. Balance q by its real-root count and the sign of d, then fill any shortfall with larger coefficient and d ranges until exactly budget unique octics are emitted.
hypotheses.label: Quadratic-quartic compositum norms
hypotheses.mission: Introduce a genuinely different algebraic construction aimed at direct-product and diagonal-pair transitive groups rather than generic wreath behavior.
hypotheses.rationale: The construction forces integer coefficients while encoding a global quadratic subfield. For linearly disjoint quartic and quadratic fields, a generic translated root generates the degree-8 compositum. Choosing quartics with different modular Galois fingerprints varies the product group, and choosing d>0 or d<0 plus quartic root geometry controls accessible signatures.

hypotheses.expected_result: High verified fraction dominated by 8T50, a useful backup route to 8T50|8, and improvements to one or more of the large incumbent field discriminants, especially 8T50|0, |4, or |6.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Reject the mechanism if its median polynomial discriminant is not substantially below the uniform baseline at comparable coefficient height, or if fresh evaluation produces neither 8T50|8 nor any field-discriminant improvement while sacrificing more than 15 percentage points of verified fraction.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Oversampling a correlated low-height coefficient lattice and ranking candidates by exact polynomial discriminant, signature scarcity, and modular transitivity will preserve the incumbent's high S8 yield while producing markedly smaller field discriminants than uniform sampling from [-20,20].
hypotheses.implementation: Generate a deterministic pool substantially larger than budget from multiple discrete-Laplace scales, sparse coefficient masks, and procedurally generated translated low-height polynomials. Compute nonzero polynomial discriminants exactly using integer resultant arithmetic, determine real-root count with Sturm sequences, and obtain finite-field factor fingerprints. Rank within each signature stratum by log absolute discriminant with diversity penalties for identical coefficient shapes and modular fingerprints. Reserve the largest quota for r=8, then r=4 and r=6, while retaining some r=0 and r=2 record attempts. Deduplicate globally, exclude a0=0, and enlarge the pool deterministically until exactly budget candidates survive.
hypotheses.label: Discriminant-ranked generic lattice sampling
hypotheses.mission: Exploit the incumbent's excellent irreducibility and verification behavior while changing its proposal distribution enough to target the missing totally real case and improve existing 8T50 discriminant records.
hypotheses.rationale: For a monogenic order, the field discriminant divides the polynomial discriminant, so low polynomial discriminant is a useful inexpensive surrogate. Discrete-Laplace coefficients, sparse perturbations, and correlations induced by translating x avoid the boundary-heavy geometry of a uniform box. Signature quotas prevent the r=0 and r=2 majority from consuming the whole budget.

hypotheses.expected_result: Broader group and signature entropy than any single arm, fresh pairs from rare reciprocal, sparse, or locally constrained families, and occasional difficult discriminant improvements from the within-cell low-discriminant ranking.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Reject the portfolio if it occupies many declared feature cells but produces no more verified group diversity than the uniform incumbent across fresh seeds. Also reject it if bookkeeping reduces the verified fraction below 50% without yielding at least one fresh missing pair.
hypotheses.hypothesis: A deterministic quality-diversity portfolio over structural feature cells will discover groups missed by each single construction because rare useful templates will receive guaranteed representation instead of being overwhelmed by high-yield S8 candidates.
hypotheses.implementation: Build a procedural grammar of monic octics including sparse trinomials and tetranomials, reciprocal lifts x^4 q(x+1/x), shifted-even forms, Eisenstein-shaped coefficient vectors, and a small generic control arm. Generate a large seed-deterministic pool over expanding parameter shells. Assign each candidate a feature tuple consisting of construction tag, Sturm signature, coefficient-height bin, discriminant bin, selected local valuation data, and modular factor fingerprints. Fill budget by round-robin novelty selection across occupied cells, ranking within a cell by low absolute polynomial discriminant and then a deterministic seed-derived tie breaker. Cap every construction tag and signature, deduplicate globally, and continue expanding shells until exactly budget valid vectors are returned.
hypotheses.label: Feature-cell structural portfolio
hypotheses.mission: Run complementary exploration that prevents any single algebraic family or easy signature from monopolizing the budget and preserves a path to difficult discriminant records.
hypotheses.rationale: With 49 entirely uncovered groups, immediate exploitation of one template is premature. Useful axes include reciprocal symmetry, even or shifted-even form, sparse support, quartic-in-x^2 form, Eisenstein local shape, Newton-polygon profile, real-root count, modular factor partitions, and discriminant scale. Selecting the best few candidates per cell turns these axes into an explicit exploration objective while still rewarding low discriminant within comparable cells.

details.thesis: The baseline's 97.4% verification rate but exclusive recovery of 8T50 shows that validity is not the bottleneck: generic coefficient sampling collapses almost entirely to S8. This generation should therefore devote most candidates to constructions that force proper block systems or compositum actions, while retaining separate, sharply targeted arms for the missing totally real 8T50 signature and low-discriminant generic fields. Every implementation must use only the supplied seed and procedural enumeration, return exactly budget unique ascending vectors [a0,...,a8] with a8=1 and a0!=0, and must not embed catalogue polynomials, known answers, or hidden seeds.
